faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.sub: Brief answers to the questions buyers and owners ask first.

commission.q: How much does the agency charge?
commission.a: For apartment sales, the fee is 5% of the sale agreement price, including VAT, and is paid only by the seller. Terms for other property types and rentals are agreed separately in writing.

documents.q: Which documents should be checked before buying?
documents.a: The exact set depends on the property. It commonly includes the current title deed, seller identity and authority, registered burdens and restrictions, planning or legalisation status, and the draft agreement. Partner lawyers and the notary carry out the relevant legal checks.

foreigners.q: Can a foreign citizen buy property in Montenegro?
foreigners.a: In many cases, yes. Restrictions can apply to certain categories of land and property, so the buyer's citizenship and the specific title deed must be checked before a deposit is paid.

residency.q: Does buying property automatically grant residence?
residency.a: No. Property may be a basis for a temporary residence application when the current statutory conditions are met, but residence is a separate procedure and is not automatic.

legalisation.q: Can an unlegalised property be sold?
legalisation.a: The answer depends on the property's registration and legalisation status and on the current law. Some transactions can be restricted. We recommend checking the title deed and obtaining legal advice before agreeing terms.

areas.q: Which parts of Montenegro do you cover?
areas.a: The agency is based in Budva and works across the coast, including the Budva Riviera, Petrovac, Tivat, Kotor, Herceg Novi and Bar. Individual investment opportunities may be located elsewhere in Montenegro.

form.title: Tell us about your plans
form.text: Describe what you are looking for or what you would like to sell, and we will get back to you the way you prefer. You can also message us directly.
